comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 continuity check; complete official curriculum table 2025-2026
comparator.sourceNotes: The current LUMC programme page and 2026-2027 Year 1 timetable confirm an active three-year Biomedical Sciences bachelor and the same first-year sequence. Live 2026-2027 Leiden module endpoints confirm the names and credits of nearly all substantive first- and second-year courses, including Immunology, Infectious Agents and Immunity, Design and Analysis of Biomedical Studies, Physiology, Hormones and the Nervous System and Human Pathology. Leiden's latest complete accessible official curriculum table is the 2025-2026 Study Guide; it accounts for exactly 180 EC and supplies the integrated skills lines and third-year allocations that are not exposed by the new live catalogue. This reconstruction preserves that exact 60+60+60 structure and records the one-year source-continuity limitation explicitly rather than inventing changes. No formal route is selected: Year 3 contains a genuine 15-EC elective or half-minor space.

questionsApplications.label: How do healthy and diseased human bodies function from molecules to organs?
How can genetic, cellular, immunological and experimental methods explain disease mechanisms?

alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, anatomy and physiology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and neuroscience with laboratory, statistical and ethical study. It reflects Leiden's clinically oriented biomedical core while UCR lacks the complete wet-lab sequence and compulsory 21-EC research placement.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest route covers human biology, molecular disease mechanisms and biomedical research. Direct target evidence then supports distinct public-health/intervention and biomedical-data/diagnostics alternatives. All three form coherent 24-course curricula, pass mechanical feasibility and differ by at least four courses per side. Production stops at the maximum of three.

notes.text: Leiden Biomedical Sciences requires a tightly integrated molecular, physiological, clinical, immunological and laboratory sequence, followed by a 21-EC Student Research Project and 15 EC of elective or half-minor space. UCR can assemble biomedical, public-health and quantitative-data programmes, but it does not duplicate Leiden's complete wet-lab sequence, clinical orientation or guaranteed research placement; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than equivalence.
